root_cause.text: The previous patch introduced a guard condition that skipped stop_streaming teardown when the instance was already in IRIS_INST_ERROR state, preventing proper cleanup of buffers and firmware state even when userspace explicitly requested stream termination.
root_cause.evidence: The revert removes the early exit check `if (inst->state == IRIS_INST_ERROR) goto exit;` that was causing stop_streaming to be skipped. The patch description explicitly states this caused two regressions: (1) buffers were not returned to vb2 because `iris_helper_buffers_done()` was skipped when in error state, and (2) firmware teardown was incomplete when sessions failed early, leaving the firmware in an inconsistent state. The fix ensures `iris_helper_buffers_done()` is always called regardless of instance state, and only the state transition to IRIS_INST_ERROR is conditional on actual errors.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove premature error state exit that prevented proper cleanup of streaming resources in error conditions.
intent_record.what: Removed a conditional check that tested if inst->state equals IRIS_INST_ERROR and jumped to the exit label if true. The two lines checking this error state condition were deleted.
intent_record.how: This change allows the function to continue executing its normal streaming stop logic even when the instance is in an ERROR state, rather than short-circuiting to the exit label. Previously, error state instances would skip the queue type validation and any other downstream operations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure buffers are always marked as errored during streaming stop, regardless of error conditions, while keeping state transition conditional on actual errors.
intent_record.what: Removed the conditional guard around iris_helper_buffers_done() call, making it execute unconditionally. The iris_helper_buffers_done() call was moved outside the 'if (ret)' block, while iris_inst_change_state() remains conditionally executed only when ret is non-zero. Added a blank line after the conditional block.
intent_record.how: Previously, buffer cleanup (iris_helper_buffers_done) only occurred when an error condition (ret != 0) was detected. Now it executes regardless of the ret value, ensuring buffers are always marked as errored when streaming stops. The state change to IRIS_INST_ERROR still only happens on actual errors, but buffer cleanup is now unconditional.

The vulnerability root cause describes a guard condition that skips stop_streaming teardown when the instance is in IRIS_INST_ERROR state. However, in this commit's iris_vb2_stop_streaming function (lines 122-147), there is NO such guard condition present. The function proceeds directly to call iris_vdec_session_streamoff() without checking for IRIS_INST_ERROR state. The only state check in this commit is in iris_vb2_buf_queue (line 157-160) which prevents queueing when in error state, but this is a different function. Since the vulnerable guard condition (skipping streamoff when IRIS_INST_ERROR) is not present in this commit, this is not the bug-introducing commit. The vulnerability must have been introduced in a different commit.
